newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel puts 3,000 West Bank homes up for sale.
newsitem.headline: Israel puts 3,000 West Bank homes up for sale.

text.p: Jewish settlers said on Sunday Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government had put about 3,000 apartments on sale for Jews in the West Bank.
The apartments were completed years ago but Israel's Labour government, ousted by Netanyahu in May, had blocked their sale.
"Prices were set for the apartments and the marketing has begun," said settler leader Aharon Domb. A government spokesman said he was checking the report.
Netanyahu, leader of the right-wing Likud party, lifted the previous government's restrictions in August but technical details held up sale of the 3,000 apartments, Domb said.
Likud opposes the Labour party's policy of swapping occupied land for peace.

Domb said demand was high for the empty apartments but many prospective buyers might wait until the government offered incentives to encourage Israelis to move to the West Bank and Gaza Strip, where about two million Palestinians live.
A previous Likud government began building the apartments in 1990 and Labour, honouring contracts with builders, completed the construction.
Palestinians say the settlements -- home to around 130,000 Jews -- are illegal under international law and the United States has said they pose an obstacle to peace.
The PLO wants to set up a state in the West Bank and Gaza which Israel captured in the 1967 Middle East war.
Netanyahu opposes Palestinian statehood and says Jews have the right to settle anywhere in the West Bank and Gaza.
